topics: Introduction: Energy Scenario: India and world
Basic concepts related to solar radiation
position of sun in the sky
position of sun with respect to the centre of the earth
Role of atmosphere on solar radiation
angle of incidence on a tilted plane
Storage of heat in solar thermal power plants
storage media and heat transfer fluids
Non-thermal routes for solar energy conversion
Fundamentals of PV: Principles and performance analysis
standalone PV system: Components and design of standalone system
grid connected PV system: components and design of grid connected PV systems
Methods of fixing power tariff - Simple Methods to Calculate the Plant Economy - Life Cycle Cost - Payback Period
Relevance of financial and economic feasibility evaluation of energy technologies and systems
Energy Policy related acts and regulation
Economic Analysis for the Selection of Alternative Decisions and the future of the Power Plants

partA.description: 2 Questions from each module.  Total of 8 Questions, each carrying 3 marks

partB.description: Each question carries 9 marks.  Two questions will be given from each module, out of which 1 question should be answered. Each question can have a maximum of 3 sub divisions.

courseOutcomes.description: Understand the basic concepts of solar radiation, the sun-earth relationship, and the effects of the atmosphere on solar energy.
Able to recall the various types of solar collectors and their theoretical principles, including flat plate collectors and concentrating collectors.
Apply thermal analysis techniques to different solar collectors and implement design principles for both standalone and grid-connected PV systems.
Understand the methods for calculating plant economy, including life cycle cost, payback period, and the relevance of economic feasibility evaluations for energy technologies.
